column1: # Release tags cut from a side branch, whose commit is therefore NOT reachable
# from main by parent links.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The Main History Drift Detector asserts that main can still reach the latest
# v* tag. That assertion is how a force-push severing main's history is caught
# within 24h (see the 2026-04-25 incident and docs/runbooks/2026-05-02-main-
# orphan-and-userhelper-flag.md). A hotfix released from an `origin/hotfix/*`
# branch violates the same assertion for an entirely legitimate reason: the
# fix reaches main as an EQUIVALENT commit, never as that commit.
# WHY IT IS A FILE AND NOT AN INFERENCE
# The tempting shortcut is to let the detector pass whenever `git cherry` or
# `git patch-id` finds an equivalent patch on main. That would defeat the
# detector: a force-push that rebased history into patch-equivalent commits
# would satisfy it and report green, which is precisely the severed-parent-link
# case the check exists to catch. patch-id is also blind to commit metadata,
# signatures and trailers, and mismatches squash-merges. So the exemption has
# to be an explicit, reviewed, committed fact — a force-push cannot add a row
# here without that addition itself being a visible commit on main.
# The recorded main-side commit is re-verified as reachable on every run, so an
# entry cannot mask a later loss of that commit either.
# FORMAT  <tag><TAB><main-side equivalent commit><TAB><note>
# Add a row when, and only when, a release is tagged on a branch that is not
# merged back into main. Prefer merging the hotfix branch into main instead;
# a row here is the fallback for releases already cut that way.
